questions.question: The SONAR technique is used to determine the:

__
 
• **Sonar** (Sound Navigation and Ranging) is a technique that uses sound propagation to navigate, communicate, or detect objects under the surface of the water.
 
• It is commonly used to **locate underwater hills** and **ice-bergs**, and to determine **the depth of the sea**.
 
• **SONAR sends out ultrasonic sound waves**
 
• **The sound waves bounce off underwater objects**
 
• **The time it takes for the sound waves to return is measured**
 
• **The distance to the object is calculated using** the speed of sound and the time it took for the sound to return

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Sonar systems are divided into two types: **active sonar** and **passive sonar**.
 
• Active sonar emits sound pulses and listens for echoes, while passive sonar listens for sound waves emitted by other sources.
 
• The use of sonar technology is critical in various fields such as **marine biology, underwater exploration, and naval warfare**.
 
• Sonar technology has advanced significantly, allowing for more precise and efficient detection and mapping of underwater environments.

questions.question: The area of the triangle formed by the line 2x - 4y - 7 = 0 with the coordinate axis is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The equation of the line is 2x - 4y - 7 = 0

**Formula used:**

The area of the triangle formed by a line with the coordinate axes is given by:

Area = dfrac{1}{2} times |x{-intercept}| times |y{-intercept}|

**Calculation:**

To find the x-intercept, set y = 0 in the line equation:

2x - 4(0) - 7 = 0

⇒ 2x - 7 = 0

⇒ 2x = 7

⇒ x = 7/2

To find the y-intercept, set x = 0 in the line equation:

2(0) - 4y - 7 = 0

⇒ -4y - 7 = 0

⇒ -4y = 7

⇒ y = -7/4

Since the intercepts are positive distances, use their magnitudes:

Area = dfrac{1}{2} times | dfrac{7}{2} | times | dfrac{7}{4} |

⇒ Area = dfrac{1}{2} times dfrac{7}{2} times dfrac{7}{4}

⇒ Area = dfrac{1}{2} times dfrac{49}{8}

⇒ Area = dfrac{49}{16} unit2

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**

questions.question: Aphelion occurs in early ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**July**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **laws of Johannes Kepler**, all planets in the Solar system have **elliptical orbits** with the Sun at one of the focal points. 
 
• Now due to this reason at times, Earth will be closer to the sun and at times it will drift far away from the sun.**​**
 
• Aphelion, in astronomy, is the point in the orbit of a planet, comet, or other body most distant from the Sun.
 
• When Earth is at its aphelion in early July, it is about 4,800,000 km (3,000,000 miles) farther from the Sun than when at its perihelion in early January. 

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/86539eebf140e1772c353d1f324f0872a0038dcfe710727344193af27cd71c1f.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The **elliptical orbit **of the **earth around the sun** is the cause for **aphelion and perihelion. **
 
• Another cause for this perihelion and aphelion may be the 23.5-degree tilt of the axis of Earth. This tilt results in the changing of the seasons.
 
• Earth's Perihelion and Aphelion:__
 __
 
• The Earth is closest to the Sun, or at the Perihelion, about 2 weeks after the December Solstice, when it is winter in the Northern Hemisphere.
 
• Conversely, the Earth is farthest away from the Sun, at the Aphelion point, 2 weeks after the June Solstice, when the Northern Hemisphere is enjoying warm summer months.
 
• Mathematicians and astronomers estimate that in the year 6430, over 4000 years from now, the timing of the Perihelion and the March Equinox will coincide. 
 
 
 
• Perigee and Apogee:__
 __
 
• Like the Earth's orbit around the Sun, the Moon's path around the Earth is elliptical. 
 
• The point in the Moon's orbit that is closest to the Earth is called the Perigee and the point farthest from the Earth is known as the Apogee.
 
• The terms are also sometimes used interchangeably with the Earth's Perihelion and Aphelion. 
 
 
 
• Perihelion:__ The Earth reaches its perihelion on January 3 every year at a distance of about 147 million km from the Sun.

questions.question: The power of accommodation of the eye usually decreases with ageing. This condition is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Presbyopia**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The defect of vision in human beings in which the power of accommodation of the eye decreases with aging and the near point gradually recedes away is known as Presbyopia.
 
• Presbyopia:
 
 
• ​The power of accommodation of the eye usually decreases with aging.
 
• For most people, the near point gradually recedes away.
 
• They find it difficult to see nearby objects comfortably and distinctly without corrective eyeglasses.
 
• **This defect is called Presbyopia. It arises due to the gradual weakening of the ciliary m**uscles and diminishing flexibility of the eye lens.
 
• Sometimes, a person may suffer from both myopia and hypermetropia.
 
• Such people often require bifocal lenses.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Hypermetropia:

 
 
• Long-sightedness, also known as hypermetropia or hyperopia is a common vision disorder.
 
• It results from the overall power of the eye not being strong enough, or the length of the eye being too short.
 
• A surgical correction is a treatment option for hypermetropia, including laser eye surgery and clear lens exchange.
 
• This defect can be corrected by using a convex lens of appropriate power.
 
 
 
• Myopia:
 
 
• ​Nearsightedness (myopia) is a common vision condition in which you can see objects near to you clearly, but objects farther away are blurry.
 
• It occurs when the shape of your eye causes light rays to bend (refract) incorrectly, focusing images in front of your retina instead of on your retina.

Number of blue balls = 5x

questions.question: The average of four consecutive even integers is 27, what is the largest of these numbers?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The average of four consecutive even integers is 27.

**Formula used:**

Let the four consecutive even integers be x, x + 2, x + 4, and x + 6.

Average = (Sum of all integers) / (Number of integers)

**Calculation:**

(x + (x + 2) + (x + 4) + (x + 6)) / 4 = 27

⇒ (4x + 12) / 4 = 27

⇒ 4x + 12 = 108

⇒ 4x = 96

⇒ x = 24

The largest number = x + 6

**∴ The correct answer is option 2.**

questions.question: How many fundamental rights were enshrined in the Constitution of India of 1950?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution, from Article 12 to 35.
 
• These rights are essential for the overall development of individuals and the preservation of human dignity.
 
• Article 21 of the Indian Constitution guarantees the Right to Life and Personal Liberty.
 
• Fundamental Rights are justiciable, meaning they can be enforced through the courts of law in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Fundamental Rights

 
 
• Fundamental Rights are the basic human rights guaranteed to all individuals by the Constitution of India. These rights are crucial for the protection and development of individuals.
 
• They are meant to promote the ideal of political democracy and prevent the arbitrary use of power by the state.
 
• Some of the key Fundamental Rights include the Right to Equality (Articles 14-18), Right to Freedom (Articles 19-22), Right against Exploitation (Articles 23-24), Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25-28), Cultural and Educational Rights (Articles 29-30), and the Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32).
 
• These rights are enforceable by the courts, and individuals can approach the judiciary to seek protection and enforcement of their Fundamental Rights.
 
 
 
• Enforcement of Fundamental Rights
 
 
• Fundamental Rights are justiciable, meaning individuals can approach the courts to enforce these rights if they are violated.
 
• The Supreme Court and High Courts have the power to issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
 
• Writs such as habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari are used to enforce these rights.
 
 
 
• Right to Life (Article 21)
 
 
• Article 21 of the Indian Constitution guarantees the Right to Life and Personal Liberty.
 
• This article ensures that no person shall be deprived of their life or personal liberty except according to the procedure established by law.
 
• The Right to Life under Article 21 has been interpreted by the Supreme Court to include various rights such as the right to live with human dignity, right to livelihood, right to health, right to education, and more.

• He may withhold his assent to the bill.
 
• He may return the bill (If it is not a Money Bill) for the reconsideration of the Parliament.

• Absolute veto, that is, withholding of assent to the bill passed by the legislature.

questions.question: All the involuntary actions, including blood pressure, salivation and vomiting are controlled by the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**medulla**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Medulla Oblongata**

 
 
• Location: The medulla oblongata is the lowermost part of the brainstem, located directly above the spinal cord.
 
• Function: It plays a crucial role in controlling vital autonomic functions such as:
 
• Respiration: Controls the rate and depth of breathing.
 
• Cardiovascular function: Regulates heart rate and blood pressure.
 
• Digestion: Influences swallowing, vomiting, and other digestive processes.
 
• Other functions: Controls sneezing, coughing, and swallowing reflexes.
 
• Structure: The medulla contains nuclei for several cranial nerves, including those involved in swallowing, tongue movement, and head and shoulder movements.
 
• Significance: Damage to the medulla can have life-threatening consequences, including respiratory failure, cardiac arrest, and loss of consciousness.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Forebrain**

 
 
• Location: The largest and most complex part of the brain, located above the midbrain and hindbrain.
 
• Function: Responsible for a wide range of complex functions, including:
 
• Sensory and motor processing: Receives and processes sensory information, and initiates voluntary movements.
 
• Higher cognitive functions: Involved in thought, language, memory, emotion, and personality.
 
• Homeostasis: Regulates body temperature, appetite, thirst, and sleep-wake cycles.
 
• Structure: Consists of two cerebral hemispheres, the thalamus, hypothalamus, and limbic system.
 
• Significance: The forebrain is essential for human consciousness, intelligence, and overall brain function.
 
 
 
• **Midbrain**
 
 
• Location: Located between the forebrain and hindbrain, forming the middle portion of the brainstem.
 
• Function: Plays a crucial role in:
 
• Motor function: Involved in controlling eye movements, posture, and balance.
 
• Sensory processing: Processes visual and auditory information.
 
• Pain perception: Plays a role in pain modulation.
 
• Arousal and consciousness: Contributes to maintaining alertness and wakefulness.
 
• Structure: Contains several important nuclei and tracts, including the substantia nigra and the red nucleus.
 
• Significance: Damage to the midbrain can result in various neurological problems, including Parkinson's disease, visual and auditory impairments, and movement disorders.
 
 
 
• **Limbic System**
 
 
• Location: A collection of interconnected brain structures located deep within the brain, beneath the cerebral cortex.
 
• Function: Plays a crucial role in:
 
• Emotions: Regulates emotions such as fear, anger, pleasure, and sadness.
 
• Memory: Involved in the formation and retrieval of memories, particularly emotional memories.
 
• Motivation: Drives basic motivations such as hunger, thirst, and sex.
 
• Learning: Plays a role in learning and habit formation.
